```
+import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
+import type { LightboxDeleteHandler } from '../types';
+
+/**
+ * Invoke a lightbox delete handler with standard error presentation.
+ * Used by ImageLightbox, VideoLightbox, and useSharedLightboxState to avoid
+ * duplicating the same try/catch + normalizeAndPresentError wrapper.
+ */
+export async function invokeLightboxDelete(
+  onDelete: LightboxDeleteHandler,
+  mediaId: string,
+  context: string,
+): Promise<void> {
+  try {
+    await Promise.resolve(onDelete(mediaId));
+  } catch (error) {
+    normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
+      context,
+      toastTitle: 'Delete Failed',
+    });
+  }
+}
```

```
1→import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
     2→
     3→type Listener = () => void;
     4→
     5→let openCount = 0;
     6→const listeners = new Set<Listener>();
     7→
     8→function notifyListeners(): void {
     9→  listeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
    10→}
    11→
    12→function getSnapshot(): boolean {
    13→  return openCount > 0;
    14→}
    15→
    16→function subscribe(listener: Listener): () => void {
    17→  listeners.add(listener);
    18→  return () => {
    19→    listeners.delete(listener);
    20→  };
    21→}
    22→
    23→export function acquireLightboxOpenState(): () => void {
    24→  openCount += 1;
    25→  notifyListeners();
    26→
    27→  let released = false;
    28→  return () => {
    29→    if (released) {
    30→      return;
    31→    }
    32→    released = true;
    33→    openCount = Math.max(0, openCount - 1);
    34→    notifyListeners();
    35→  };
    36→}
    37→
    38→export function useLightboxOpenState(): boolean {
    39→  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getSnapshot);
    40→}
    41→
    42→function __resetLightboxOpenStateForTests(): void {
    43→  openCount = 0;
    44→  notifyListeners();
    45→}
    46→
```

```
    99→/**
   100→ * Check if all sibling segments are complete and mark orchestrator done if so
   101→ */
   102→export async function checkOrchestratorCompletion(
   103→  params: CheckOrchestratorCompletionParams,
   104→): Promise<void> {
   105→  const {
   106→    supabase,
   107→    taskIdString,
   108→    completedTask,
   109→    publicUrl,
   110→    supabaseUrl,
   111→    serviceKey,
   112→    logger,
   113→  } = params;
   114→  assertCompletionAuthContext(params.authContext, 'checkOrchestratorCompletion');
   115→  try {
   116→    const taskType = completedTask.task_type;
   117→    const config = taskType ? SEGMENT_TYPE_CONFIG[taskType] : null;
   118→    if (!config) {
   119→      return; // Not a segment task
   120→    }
   121→    const orchestratorTaskId = extractOrchestratorTaskId(completedTask.params, 'OrchestratorComplete');
   122→    const orchestratorRunId = extractOrchestratorRunId(completedTask.params, 'OrchestratorComplete');
   123→    if (!orchestratorTaskId) {
   124→      return;
   125→    }
   126→    const segmentTypeToQuery = config.isFinalStep
   127→      ? (config.billingSegmentType || config.segmentType)
   128→      : config.segmentType;
   129→    const orchPromise: Promise<{ data: OrchestratorTask | null; error: unknown }> =
   130→      supabase.from("tasks").select("id, status, params, result_data").eq("id", orchestratorTaskId).single();
   131→    const [orchResult, allSegments] = await Promise.all([
   132→      orchPromise,
   133→      findSiblingSegments(supabase, segmentTypeToQuery, completedTask.project_id, orchestratorTaskId, orchestratorRunId),
   134→    ]);
   135→    const { data: orchestratorTask, error: orchError } = orchResult;
   136→    if (orchError) {
   137→      throw new CompletionError({
   138→        code: 'orchestrator_fetch_failed',
   139→        context: 'checkOrchestratorCompletion',
   140→        recoverable: true,
   141→        message: `[OrchestratorComplete] Error fetching orchestrator task ${orchestratorTaskId}`,
   142→        metadata: {
   143→          orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   144→          fetch_error: orchError instanceof Error ? orchError.message : String(orchError),
   145→        },
   146→        cause: orchError,
   147→      });
   148→    }
   149→    if (!orchestratorTask) {
   150→      return;
   151→    }
   152→    if (orchestratorTask.status === 'Complete') {
   153→      return;
   154→    }
   155→    if (config.isFinalStep) {
   156→      await markOrchestratorComplete(
   157→        {
   158→          supabase,
   159→          orchestratorTask,
   160→          orchestratorTaskId,
   161→          allSegments,
   162→          publicUrl,
   163→          isFinalStep: true,
   164→          supabaseUrl,
   165→          serviceKey,
   166→        },
   167→      );
   168→      return;
   169→    }
   170→    const expectedSegmentCountResolution = resolveExpectedSegmentCount(
   171→      taskType,
   172→      orchestratorTask.params,
   173→    );
   174→    if (expectedSegmentCountResolution.invalid) {
   175→      throw new CompletionError({
   176→        code: 'orchestrator_expected_segment_count_invalid',
   177→        context: 'checkOrchestratorCompletion',
   178→        recoverable: false,
   179→        message: `Invalid expected segment count contract for orchestrator ${orchestratorTaskId}`,
   180→        metadata: {
   181→          orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   182→          task_type: taskType,
   183→          source: expectedSegmentCountResolution.source ?? 'unknown',
   184→          raw_value: expectedSegmentCountResolution.raw ?? null,
   185→        },
   186→      });
   187→    }
   188→    const segmentStats = summarizeSegmentCompletion(allSegments);
   189→    const segmentGate = evaluateSegmentCompletionGate(
   190→      expectedSegmentCountResolution.value,
   191→      segmentStats,
   192→    );
   193→    if (segmentGate.kind === 'wait') {
   194→      return;
   195→    }
   196→    if (segmentGate.kind === 'fail') {
   197→      if (segmentGate.reason === 'segments_failed') {
   198→        await markOrchestratorFailed(
   199→          supabase,
   200→          orchestratorTaskId,
   201→          segmentGate.failedSegments,
   202→          segmentGate.foundSegments,
   203→          undefined,
   204→          logger,
   205→        );
   206→      } else {
   207→        await markOrchestratorFailed(
   208→          supabase,
   209→          orchestratorTaskId,
   210→          0,
   211→          segmentGate.expectedSegments,
   212→          `Only ${segmentGate.foundSegments} of ${segmentGate.expectedSegments} expected segments were found`,
   213→          logger,
   214→        );
   215→      }
   216→      return;
   217→    }
   218→    if (config.waitForFinalStepType) {
   219→      const finalStitchStatus = await checkFinalStitchStatus(
   220→        supabase,
   221→        config.waitForFinalStepType,
   222→        completedTask.project_id,
   223→        orchestratorTaskId,
   224→        orchestratorRunId,
   225→      );
   226→      switch (finalStitchStatus) {
   227→        case 'pending':
   228→          return;
   229→        case 'failed':
   230→          await markOrchestratorFailed(supabase, orchestratorTaskId, 1, 1, undefined, logger);
   231→          return;
   232→        case 'unknown':
   233→          logger?.warn('Final-step status could not be classified; waiting before orchestrator completion', {
   234→            orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   235→            final_step_type: config.waitForFinalStepType,
   236→            orchestrator_run_id: orchestratorRunId,
   237→          });
   238→          return;
   239→        case 'complete':
   240→        case 'not_found':
   241→          break;
   242→      }
   243→    }
   244→    await markOrchestratorComplete(
   245→      {
   246→        supabase,
   247→        orchestratorTask,
   248→        orchestratorTaskId,
   249→        allSegments,
   250→        publicUrl,
   251→        isFinalStep: false,
   252→        supabaseUrl,
   253→        serviceKey,
   254→        logger,
   255→      },
   256→    );
   257→  } catch (error) {
   258→    throw toCompletionError(error, {
   259→      code: 'orchestrator_completion_failed',
   260→      context: 'checkOrchestratorCompletion',
   261→      recoverable: true,
   262→      message: `[OrchestratorComplete] Completion flow failed for task ${taskIdString}`,
   263→      metadata: {
   264→        task_id: taskIdString,
   265→        task_type: completedTask.task_type,
   266→        project_id: completedTask.project_id,
   267→      },
   268→    });
   269→  }
   270→}
   271→/**
   272→ * Find sibling segment tasks using run_id (preferred) or orchestrator_task_id (fallback)
   273→ */
   274→async function findSiblingSegments(
   275→  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   276→  segmentType: string,
   277→  projectId: string,
   278→  orchestratorTaskId: string,
   279→  orchestratorRunId: string | null
   280→): Promise<SegmentTask[]> {
   281→  if (orchestratorRunId) {
   282→    const runIdRows = await lookupTasksByRunIdWithFallback<SegmentTask>({
   283→      supabase,
   284→      taskType: segmentType,
   285→      projectId,
   286→      select: "id, status, generation_started_at",
   287→      runId: orchestratorRunId,
   288→      contextLabel: 'OrchestratorComplete',
   289→    });
   290→    if (runIdRows.length > 0) {
   291→      return runIdRows;
   292→    }
   293→  }
   294→  const orchestratorRows = await lookupTasksByOrchestratorIdWithFallback<SegmentTask>({
   295→    supabase,
   296→    taskType: segmentType,
   297→    projectId,
   298→    select: "id, status, generation_started_at",
   299→    orchestratorTaskId,
   300→    contextLabel: 'OrchestratorComplete',
   301→  });
   302→  return orchestratorRows;
   303→}
   304→/**
   305→ * Check the status of the final stitch task for this orchestrator
   306→ */
   307→async function checkFinalStitchStatus(
   308→  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   309→  finalStepType: string,
   310→  projectId: string,
   311→  orchestratorTaskId: string,
   312→  orchestratorRunId: string | null,
   313→): Promise<'not_found' | 'pending' | 'complete' | 'failed' | 'unknown'> {
   314→  let finalStepTasks: Array<{ id: string; status: string }> = [];
   315→  if (orchestratorRunId) {
   316→    finalStepTasks = await lookupTasksByRunIdWithFallback<{ id: string; status: string }>({
   317→      supabase,
   318→      taskType: finalStepType,
   319→      projectId,
   320→      select: "id, status",
   321→      runId: orchestratorRunId,
   322→      contextLabel: 'OrchestratorComplete',
   323→    });
   324→  }
   325→  if (finalStepTasks.length === 0) {
   326→    finalStepTasks = await lookupTasksByOrchestratorIdWithFallback<{ id: string; status: string }>({
   327→      supabase,
   328→      taskType: finalStepType,
   329→      projectId,
   330→      select: "id, status",
   331→      orchestratorTaskId,
   332→      contextLabel: 'OrchestratorComplete',
   333→    });
   334→  }
   335→  if (!finalStepTasks || finalStepTasks.length === 0) {
   336→    return 'not_found';
   337→  }
   338→  if (finalStepTasks.some((task) => isFailureStatus(task.status))) {
   339→    return 'failed';
   340→  }
   341→  if (finalStepTasks.some((task) => task.status === 'Complete')) {
   342→    return 'complete';
   343→  }
   344→  if (finalStepTasks.some((task) => task.status === 'Queued' || task.status === 'In Progress')) {
   345→    return 'pending';
   346→  }
   347→  return 'unknown';
   348→}
   349→/**
   350→ * Mark orchestrator as Failed
   351→ */
   352→async function markOrchestratorFailed(
   353→  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   354→  orchestratorTaskId: string,
   355→  failedSegments: number,
   356→  totalSegments: number,
   357→  errorMessage?: string,
   358→  logger?: {
   359→    warn: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
   360→    error: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
   361→  },
   362→): Promise<void> {
   363→  const { data: updatedRows, error: updateOrchError } = await supabase
   364→    .from("tasks")
   365→    .update({
   366→      status: "Failed",
   367→      error_message: errorMessage ?? `${failedSegments} of ${totalSegments} segments failed`,
   368→      generation_processed_at: new Date().toISOString()
   369→    })
   370→    .eq("id", orchestratorTaskId)
   371→    .in("status", ["Queued", "In Progress"])
   372→    .select('id');
   373→  if (updateOrchError) {
   374→    throw new CompletionError({
   375→      code: 'orchestrator_mark_failed_update_failed',
   376→      context: 'markOrchestratorFailed',
   377→      recoverable: true,
   378→      message: `[OrchestratorComplete] Failed to mark orchestrator ${orchestratorTaskId} as Failed`,
   379→      metadata: {
   380→        orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   381→        update_error: updateOrchError instanceof Error
   382→          ? updateOrchError.message
   383→          : String(updateOrchError),
   384→      },
   385→      cause: updateOrchError,
   386→    });
   387→  }
   388→  const transitionedRows = (updatedRows ?? []) as TaskUpdateRow[];
   389→  if (transitionedRows.length === 0) {
   390→    logger?.warn('Orchestrator already terminal while marking failed', {
   391→      orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   392→      failed_segments: failedSegments,
   393→      total_segments: totalSegments,
   394→    });
   395→  }
   396→}
   397→/**
   398→ * Mark orchestrator as Complete and trigger billing
   399→ */
   400→async function markOrchestratorComplete(
   401→  params: {
   402→    supabase: SupabaseClient;
   403→    orchestratorTask: OrchestratorTask;
   404→    orchestratorTaskId: string;
   405→    allSegments: SegmentTask[];
   406→    publicUrl: string;
   407→    isFinalStep: boolean;
   408→    supabaseUrl: string;
   409→    serviceKey: string;
   410→    logger?: {
   411→      warn: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
   412→      error: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
   413→    };
   414→  },
   415→): Promise<void> {
   416→  const {
   417→    supabase,
   418→    orchestratorTask,
   419→    orchestratorTaskId,
   420→    allSegments,
   421→    publicUrl,
   422→    isFinalStep,
   423→    supabaseUrl,
   424→    serviceKey,
   425→    logger,
   426→  } = params;
   427→  let earliestStartTime: string | null = null;
   428→  for (const segment of allSegments) {
   429→    if (segment.generation_started_at) {
   430→      if (!earliestStartTime || segment.generation_started_at < earliestStartTime) {
   431→        earliestStartTime = segment.generation_started_at;
   432→      }
   433→    }
   434→  }
   435→  const updateData: Record<string, unknown> = {
   436→    status: "Complete",
   437→    generation_started_at: earliestStartTime || new Date().toISOString(),
   438→    generation_processed_at: new Date().toISOString()
   439→  };
   440→  if (isFinalStep) {
   441→    updateData.output_location = publicUrl;
   442→  }
   443→  const { data: updatedRows, error: updateOrchError } = await supabase
   444→    .from("tasks")
   445→    .update(updateData)
   446→    .eq("id", orchestratorTaskId)
   447→    .in("status", ["Queued", "In Progress"])
   448→    .select('id');
   449→  if (updateOrchError) {
   450→    throw new CompletionError({
   451→      code: 'orchestrator_mark_complete_update_failed',
   452→      context: 'markOrchestratorComplete',
   453→      recoverable: true,
   454→      message: `[OrchestratorComplete] Failed to mark orchestrator ${orchestratorTaskId} as Complete`,
   455→      metadata: {
   456→        orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   457→        update_error: updateOrchError instanceof Error
   458→          ? updateOrchError.message
   459→          : String(updateOrchError),
   460→      },
   461→      cause: updateOrchError,
   462→    });
   463→  }
   464→  const transitionedRows = (updatedRows ?? []) as TaskUpdateRow[];
   465→  if (transitionedRows.length === 0) {
   466→    logger?.warn('Orchestrator already in terminal status; skipping billing side effects', {
   467→      orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   468→    });
   469→    return;
   470→  }
   471→  const billingResult = await triggerCostCalculation({
   472→    supabaseUrl,
   473→    serviceKey,
   474→    taskId: orchestratorTaskId,
   475→    logTag: 'OrchestratorComplete',
   476→  });
   477→  const existingResultData = asObjectOrEmpty(orchestratorTask.result_data);
   478→  const billingDecision = classifyBillingOutcome(billingResult);
   479→  const billingOutcome = buildBillingOutcome(billingResult, billingDecision);
   480→  await persistBillingOutcome(
   481→    supabase,
   482→    orchestratorTaskId,
   483→    existingResultData,
   484→    billingOutcome,
   485→    billingDecision,
   486→    logger,
   487→  );
   488→  if (billingDecision.reconciliationRequired) {
   489→    logger?.warn('Billing requires reconciliation policy follow-up', {
   490→      orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   491→      billing_decision: billingDecision,
   492→      billing_result: billingResult,
   493→    });
   494→  }
   495→}
   496→
```

```
   122→const ImageResourceItem: React.FC<ResourceItemProps> = ({

   181→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   185→interface ResourceBrowserGridProps {

   190→export const ResourceBrowserGrid: React.FC<ResourceBrowserGridProps> = ({

   246→      {browsing.paginatedResources.map((resource) => {
   247→        const legacyOwnerId =
   248→          'user_id' in resource && typeof resource.user_id === 'string' ? resource.user_id : undefined;

   264→        if (browsing.isVideoMode) {
```

```
    49→export function useResourceBrowserData({
```

```
1→import { useEffect, useMemo } from 'react';
     2→import { getQuantizedGap, quantizeTotalFrames } from '../utils';
     3→
     4→const STANDARD_MAX_TOTAL = 81;
     5→const STANDARD_MAX_CONTEXT = 30;
     6→
     7→interface UseJoinClipsSettingsControllerParams {
     8→  gapFrames: number;
     9→  setGapFrames: (val: number) => void;
    10→  contextFrames: number;
    11→  setContextFrames: (val: number) => void;
    12→  replaceMode: boolean;
    13→  shortestClipFrames?: number;
    14→  keepBridgingImagesValue: boolean;
    15→  setKeepBridgingImages?: (val: boolean) => void;
    16→}
    17→
    18→interface JoinClipsSettingsController {
    19→  maxGapFrames: number;
    20→  maxContextFrames: number;
    21→  minClipFramesRequired: number;
    22→  actualTotal: number;
    23→  quantizedTotal: number;
    24→  handleContextFramesChange: (val: number) => void;
    25→  sliderNumber: (value: number | readonly number[]) => number;
    26→}
    27→
    28→export function useJoinClipsSettingsController({
    29→  gapFrames,
    30→  setGapFrames,
    31→  contextFrames,
    32→  setContextFrames,
    33→  replaceMode,
    34→  shortestClipFrames,
    35→  keepBridgingImagesValue,
    36→  setKeepBridgingImages,
    37→}: UseJoinClipsSettingsControllerParams): JoinClipsSettingsController {
    38→  const { maxGapFrames, maxContextFrames, minClipFramesRequired } = useMemo(() => {
    39→    const minRequired = replaceMode
    40→      ? gapFrames + 2 * contextFrames
    41→      : contextFrames;
    42→
    43→    if (!shortestClipFrames || shortestClipFrames <= 0) {
    44→      const defaultMaxGap = Math.max(1, STANDARD_MAX_TOTAL - contextFrames * 2);
    45→      return {
    46→        maxGapFrames: defaultMaxGap,
    47→        maxContextFrames: STANDARD_MAX_CONTEXT,
    48→        minClipFramesRequired: minRequired,
    49→      };
    50→    }
    51→
    52→    if (replaceMode) {
    53→      const maxGapForClip = Math.max(1, shortestClipFrames - 2 * contextFrames);
    54→      const maxGapForTotal = Math.max(1, STANDARD_MAX_TOTAL - contextFrames * 2);
    55→      let finalMaxGap = Math.min(maxGapForClip, maxGapForTotal);
    56→      finalMaxGap = Math.max(1, Math.floor((finalMaxGap - 1) / 4) * 4 + 1);
    57→
    58→      const maxContextForClip = Math.floor((shortestClipFrames - gapFrames) / 2);
    59→      const maxContextForTotal = Math.floor((STANDARD_MAX_TOTAL - gapFrames) / 2);
    60→      const finalMaxContext = Math.max(
    61→        4,
    62→        Math.min(maxContextForClip, maxContextForTotal, STANDARD_MAX_CONTEXT),
    63→      );
    64→
    65→      return {
    66→        maxGapFrames: Math.max(1, finalMaxGap),
    67→        maxContextFrames: finalMaxContext,
    68→        minClipFramesRequired: minRequired,
    69→      };
    70→    }
    71→
    72→    const maxContextForClip = shortestClipFrames;
    73→    const finalMaxContext = Math.max(
    74→      4,
    75→      Math.min(maxContextForClip, STANDARD_MAX_CONTEXT),
    76→    );
    77→    const maxGapForTotal = Math.max(1, STANDARD_MAX_TOTAL - contextFrames * 2);
    78→
    79→    return {
    80→      maxGapFrames: maxGapForTotal,
    81→      maxContextFrames: finalMaxContext,
    82→      minClipFramesRequired: minRequired,
    83→    };
    84→  }, [shortestClipFrames, contextFrames, gapFrames, replaceMode]);
    85→
    86→  useEffect(() => {
    87→    if (gapFrames > maxGapFrames) {
    88→      setGapFrames(getQuantizedGap(maxGapFrames, contextFrames));
    89→    }
    90→  }, [maxGapFrames, gapFrames, contextFrames, setGapFrames]);
    91→
    92→  useEffect(() => {
    93→    if (contextFrames > maxContextFrames) {
    94→      setContextFrames(maxContextFrames);
    95→    }
    96→  }, [maxContextFrames, contextFrames, setContextFrames]);
    97→
    98→  useEffect(() => {
    99→    if (gapFrames <= 8 && keepBridgingImagesValue) {
   100→      setKeepBridgingImages?.(false);
   101→    }
   102→  }, [gapFrames, keepBridgingImagesValue, setKeepBridgingImages]);
   103→
   104→  const handleContextFramesChange = (val: number) => {
   105→    setContextFrames(Math.max(4, val));
   106→  };
   107→
   108→  const sliderNumber = (value: number | readonly number[]): number => {
   109→    if (typeof value === 'number') {
   110→      return value;
   111→    }
   112→    return value[0] ?? 0;
   113→  };
   114→
   115→  const actualTotal = contextFrames * 2 + gapFrames;
   116→  const quantizedTotal = quantizeTotalFrames(actualTotal);
   117→
   118→  return {
   119→    maxGapFrames,
   120→    maxContextFrames,
   121→    minClipFramesRequired,
   122→    actualTotal,
   123→    quantizedTotal,
   124→    handleContextFramesChange,
   125→    sliderNumber,
   126→  };
   127→}
   128→
```

```
1→import type { ClipPairInfo } from '@/shared/components/JoinClipsSettingsForm/types';
     2→
     3→interface ClipFrameCalculationsParams {
     4→  gapFrames: number;
     5→  contextFrames: number;
     6→  replaceMode: boolean;
     7→  selectedPair?: ClipPairInfo;
     8→}
     9→
    10→export interface ClipFrameCalculations {
    11→  totalFrames: number;
    12→  anchor1Idx: number;
    13→  anchor2Idx: number;
    14→  clipAKeptFrames: number | null;
    15→  clipBKeptFrames: number | null;
    16→  totalGenerationFlex: number;
    17→  contextFlex: number;
    18→  clipAKeptFlex: number;
    19→  clipBKeptFlex: number;
    20→  generationWindowLeftPct: number;
    21→  generationWindowWidthPct: number;
    22→}
    23→
    24→function toPercent(value: number, total: number): number {
    25→  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || !Number.isFinite(total) || total <= 0) {
    26→    return 0;
    27→  }
    28→  return (value / total) * 100;
    29→}
    30→
    31→export function getClipFrameCalculations({
    32→  gapFrames,
    33→  contextFrames,
    34→  replaceMode,
    35→  selectedPair,
    36→}: ClipFrameCalculationsParams): ClipFrameCalculations {
    37→  const totalFrames = contextFrames + gapFrames + contextFrames;
    38→  const anchor1Idx = Math.floor(gapFrames / 3);
    39→  const anchor2Idx = Math.floor((gapFrames * 2) / 3);
    40→
    41→  const gapPortion = Math.ceil(gapFrames / 2);
    42→  const framesUsedFromClipA = replaceMode
    43→    ? contextFrames + gapPortion
    44→    : contextFrames;
    45→  const framesUsedFromClipB = replaceMode
    46→    ? contextFrames + Math.floor(gapFrames / 2)
    47→    : contextFrames;
    48→
    49→  const clipAKeptFrames = selectedPair
    50→    ? Math.max(0, selectedPair.clipA.frameCount - framesUsedFromClipA)
    51→    : null;
    52→  const clipBKeptFrames = selectedPair
    53→    ? Math.max(0, selectedPair.clipB.frameCount - framesUsedFromClipB)
    54→    : null;
    55→
    56→  const totalGenerationFlex = replaceMode ? totalFrames : gapFrames;
    57→  const contextFlex = contextFrames;
    58→  const clipAKeptFlex = totalGenerationFlex / 2;
    59→  const clipBKeptFlex = totalGenerationFlex / 2;
    60→
    61→  const replaceTotalFlex = clipAKeptFlex + totalGenerationFlex + clipBKeptFlex;
    62→  const insertTotalFlex =
    63→    clipAKeptFlex + contextFlex + totalGenerationFlex + contextFlex + clipBKeptFlex;
    64→
    65→  const generationWindowLeftPct = replaceMode
    66→    ? toPercent(clipAKeptFlex, replaceTotalFlex)
    67→    : toPercent(clipAKeptFlex, insertTotalFlex);
    68→  const generationWindowWidthPct = replaceMode
    69→    ? toPercent(totalGenerationFlex, replaceTotalFlex)
    70→    : toPercent(contextFlex + totalGenerationFlex + contextFlex, insertTotalFlex);
    71→
    72→  return {
    73→    totalFrames,
    74→    anchor1Idx,
    75→    anchor2Idx,
    76→    clipAKeptFrames,
    77→    clipBKeptFrames,
    78→    totalGenerationFlex,
    79→    contextFlex,
    80→    clipAKeptFlex,
    81→    clipBKeptFlex,
    82→    generationWindowLeftPct,
    83→    generationWindowWidthPct,
    84→  };
    85→}
    86→
```

```
1→/**
     2→ * Core generation CRUD operations
     3→ * Basic database operations for generations and variants
     4→ */
     5→
     6→import type { SupabaseClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.39.7';
     7→
     8→type ExistingGenerationLookupErrorCode =
     9→  | 'existing_generation_lookup_failed'
    10→  | 'existing_generation_lookup_duplicate';
    11→
    12→export class ExistingGenerationLookupError extends Error {
    13→  readonly code: ExistingGenerationLookupErrorCode;
    14→  readonly details?: Record<string, unknown>;
    15→
    16→  constructor(
    17→    code: ExistingGenerationLookupErrorCode,
    18→    message: string,
    19→    details?: Record<string, unknown>,
    20→  ) {
    21→    super(message);
    22→    this.name = 'ExistingGenerationLookupError';
    23→    this.code = code;
    24→    this.details = details;
    25→  }
    26→}
    27→
    28→// ===== HELPERS =====
    29→
    30→/**
    31→ * Helper to safely extract value from array by index
    32→ */
    33→export function extractFromArray(arr: unknown[], index: number): unknown | undefined {
    34→  if (Array.isArray(arr) && index >= 0 && index < arr.length) {
    35→    return arr[index];
    36→  }
    37→  return undefined;
    38→}
    39→
    40→// ===== GENERATION LOOKUP =====
    41→
    42→/**
    43→ * Check for existing generation referencing this task_id
    44→ */
    45→export async function findExistingGeneration(supabase: SupabaseClient, taskId: string): Promise<unknown | null> {
    46→  try {
    47→    const { data, error } = await supabase
    48→      .from('generations')
    49→      .select('*')
    50→      .contains('tasks', JSON.stringify([taskId]))
    51→      .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
    52→      .limit(2);
    53→
    54→    if (error) {
    55→      throw new ExistingGenerationLookupError(
    56→        'existing_generation_lookup_failed',
    57→        `Failed to lookup existing generation for task ${taskId}: ${error.message}`,
    58→        {
    59→          taskId,
    60→          errorCode: error.code,
    61→          errorMessage: error.message,
    62→        },
    63→      );
    64→    }
    65→
    66→    if (!Array.isArray(data) || data.length === 0) {
    67→      return null;
    68→    }
    69→
    70→    if (data.length > 1) {
    71→      const generationIds = data
    72→        .map((row) => (typeof row === 'object' && row !== null && 'id' in row ? String((row as { id: unknown }).id) : null))
    73→        .filter((id): id is string => Boolean(id));
    74→
    75→      throw new ExistingGenerationLookupError(
    76→        'existing_generation_lookup_duplicate',
    77→        `Multiple existing generations found for task ${taskId}`,
    78→        {
    79→          taskId,
    80→          generationIds,
    81→        },
    82→      );
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    return data[0];
    86→  } catch (error) {
    87→    if (error instanceof ExistingGenerationLookupError) {
    88→      throw error;
    89→    }
    90→    throw new ExistingGenerationLookupError(
    91→      'existing_generation_lookup_failed',
    92→      `Exception while looking up existing generation for task ${taskId}`,
    93→      {
    94→        taskId,
    95→        cause: String(error),
    96→      },
    97→    );
    98→  }
    99→}
   100→
```

```
1→import type { SupabaseClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.39.7';
     2→import { edgeErrorResponse } from "../_shared/edgeRequest.ts";
     3→
     4→export interface TaskContext {
     5→  id: string;
     6→  task_type: string;
     7→  project_id: string;
     8→  params: Record<string, unknown>;
     9→  result_data: unknown;
    10→  tool_type: string;
    11→  category: string;
    12→  content_type: 'image' | 'video';
    13→  variant_type: string | null;
    14→}
    15→
    16→export type CompletionFollowUpStep =
    17→  | 'validation'
    18→  | 'orchestrator_completion'
    19→  | 'cost_calculation'
    20→  | 'follow_up_persistence';
    21→
    22→export interface CompletionFollowUpIssue {
    23→  step: CompletionFollowUpStep;
    24→  code: string;
    25→  message: string;
    26→}
    27→
    28→function defaultErrorCode(status: number): string {
    29→  if (status === 401) return 'authentication_failed';
    30→  if (status === 403) return 'forbidden';
    31→  if (status === 404) return 'not_found';
    32→  if (status === 405) return 'method_not_allowed';
    33→  if (status === 429) return 'rate_limited';
    34→  if (status === 503) return 'service_unavailable';
    35→  if (status >= 500) return 'internal_server_error';
    36→  return 'request_failed';
    37→}
    38→
    39→export function completeTaskErrorResponse(
    40→  message: string,
    41→  status: number,
    42→  errorCode = defaultErrorCode(status),
    43→): Response {
    44→  return edgeErrorResponse(
    45→    {
    46→      errorCode,
    47→      message,
    48→      recoverable: status >= 500 || status === 429,
    49→    },
    50→    status,
    51→  );
    52→}
    53→
    54→function asObjectRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {
    55→  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {
    56→    return {};
    57→  }
    58→  return value as Record<string, unknown>;
    59→}
    60→
    61→/**
    62→ * Best-effort mark a task as Failed so the UI can update immediately.
    63→ * Swallows errors — callers still return their own HTTP error response.
    64→ */
    65→export async function markTaskFailed(
    66→  supabase: SupabaseClient,
    67→  taskId: string,
    68→  errorMessage: string,
    69→): Promise<void> {
    70→  try {
    71→    await supabase.from("tasks").update({
    72→      status: "Failed",
    73→      error_message: errorMessage,
    74→      updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    75→    }).eq("id", taskId).in("status", ["Queued", "In Progress"]);
    76→  } catch {
    77→    // Best-effort — don't mask the original error
    78→  }
    79→}
    80→
    81→export async function persistCompletionFollowUpIssues(
    82→  supabase: SupabaseClient,
    83→  taskId: string,
    84→  existingResultData: unknown,
    85→  issues: CompletionFollowUpIssue[],
    86→): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; error: unknown }> {
    87→  if (issues.length === 0) {
    88→    return { ok: true };
    89→  }
    90→
    91→  const baseResultData = asObjectRecord(existingResultData);
    92→  const completionFollowUp = {
    93→    status: 'degraded',
    94→    recorded_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    95→    issues,
    96→  };
    97→
    98→  const { error } = await supabase
    99→    .from('tasks')
   100→    .update({
   101→      result_data: {
   102→        ...baseResultData,
   103→        completion_follow_up: completionFollowUp,
   104→      },
   105→    })
   106→    .eq('id', taskId);
   107→
   108→  if (error) {
   109→    return { ok: false, error };
   110→  }
   111→
   112→  return { ok: true };
   113→}
   114→
   115→/**
   116→ * Fetch task context with all required fields for the completion flow.
   117→ * Uses a single query with FK join (tasks.task_type -> task_types.name).
   118→ * Returns null if task not found or on error.
   119→ */
   120→export async function fetchTaskContext(
   121→  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   122→  taskId: string,
   123→  logger?: {
   124→    error: (message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
   125→  },
   126→): Promise<TaskContext | null> {
   127→  const { data: task, error } = await supabase
   128→    .from("tasks")
   129→    .select(`id, task_type, project_id, params, result_data, task_types!tasks_task_type_fkey(tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type)`)
   130→    .eq("id", taskId)
   131→    .single();
   132→
   133→  if (error || !task) {
   134→    logger?.error('Failed to fetch task context', {
   135→      task_id: taskId,
   136→      fetch_error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
   137→    });
   138→    return null;
   139→  }
   140→
   141→  const taskTypeInfo = task.task_types || {};
   142→
   143→  return {
   144→    id: task.id,
   145→    task_type: task.task_type,
   146→    project_id: task.project_id,
   147→    params: task.params || {},
   148→    result_data: task.result_data,
   149→    tool_type: taskTypeInfo.tool_type || 'unknown',
   150→    category: taskTypeInfo.category || 'unknown',
   151→    content_type: taskTypeInfo.content_type || 'image',
   152→    variant_type: taskTypeInfo.variant_type || null,
   153→  };
   154→}
   155→
```

```
    19→export function useClipPersistence({

    23→  settingsLoaded,
```

```
    42→    let scrollTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    43→
    44→    const handleScroll = () => {
    45→      setIsScrolling(true);
    46→      if (scrollTimer) {
    47→        clearTimeout(scrollTimer);
    48→      }
    49→      scrollTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    50→        setIsScrolling(false);
    51→        scrollTimer = null;
    52→      }, 200);

    54→

    79→    const items = Array.from(event.dataTransfer.items);

   149→    }

   153→      transitionPrompts,

   155→      over.id,

   160→  }, [clips, setClips, setTransitionPrompts, transitionPrompts]);

   162→  return {

   164→    handleDragEnd,
   165→    handleDragEnter,
```

Excellent. Now I have enough data to provide a comprehensive review. Let me compile my findings:

## Review of Travel-Between-Images Tool Changes (branch vs main)

This is a **significant refactoring** involving 309 files changed with 13,259 insertions and 9,466 deletions. Here are my detailed findings:

### CRITICAL ISSUES FOUND

#### 1. **Over-Decomposition: "Model" Hooks Are Thin Passthroughs** ❌
Multiple new "model" hooks have been extracted that are essentially field-mapping wrappers:

- **`useGenerationControllerInputModel.ts` (182 lines)** - Maps scattered settings into a single object for `useGenerationController`. This is a *passthrough wrapper* that:
  - Takes 10+ sliced parameters
  - Returns them reassembled in a useMemo
  - Adds zero business logic, just reorganizes fields
  - This pattern repeats across `useShotEditorApplySettingsModel.ts`, `useShotEditorLayoutPayloadModel.ts` (340 lines)

**Impact**: Adds layers of indirection without semantic benefit. Readers must trace through multiple hook files to understand data flow. The object transformation could happen inline.

- **`useShotEditorLayoutModel.ts` (52 lines)** - Just calls `useShotSettingsValue()` and returns a reassembled object. Pure overhead.

- **`useShotEditorMediaAndOutputControllers.ts` (72 lines)** - Returns destructured output from two other controllers without adding logic.

#### 2. **Structural Reorganization Without Functional Benefit** ⚠️
Large files were reorganized into subdirectories rather than functionally decomposed:

- **Moved ~70+ hooks into categorical subdirectories** (navigation/, settings/, timeline/, video/, workflow/, actions/, editor-state/, segment/, drag/)
- This is a **folder-based taxonomy**, not semantic decomposition
- Example: `Timeline/hooks/` now has `timeline-core/`, `segment/`, `drag/` - creating 3 levels of nesting for hooks that were previously flat
- **Result**: More file path depth without clearer separation of concerns

#### 3. **Index File Deletions Break Discoverability** ❌
Removed 5+ barrel export files:

- `src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/index.ts` (deleted)
- `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/index.ts` (deleted)  
- `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/sections/index.ts` (deleted)
- `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/state/index.ts` (deleted)

**Impact**: 
- Developers must now know exact hook filenames and import paths
- No single place to see "what hooks exist in ShotEditor"
- Migration path unclear for anyone using old barrel exports (breaking change)
- Per CLAUDE.md: "don't create catalog docs" — but this destroyed a functional catalog

#### 4. **Large Extraction Without Validation of Responsibility** ⚠️
`useBatchGuidanceVideoController.ts` (289 lines) extracted from `BatchGuidanceVideo.tsx` (514 → 259 lines):

- Hook is 289 lines with ~15 refs, 8+ useState/useCallback/useEffect calls, frame calculation logic, AND video upload orchestration
- **Unclear single responsibility**: manages video upload, frame scrubbing, drag-drop UI state, and canvas rendering logic
- The extracted hook doesn't reduce the component's cognitive load (component is still aware of all this state)
- **No behavioral change**, but harder to debug (ref chain: component → controller → multiple refs + effects)

#### 5. **Potential Behavioral Risk: Removed Service Modules** ⚠️
Deleted without clear migration path:

- `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/services/generateVideo/repository.ts`
- `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/services/generateVideo/resolution.ts`  
- `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/services/generateVideo/structureGuidance.ts`

These were ~40-60 lines each. **Risk**: If they contained business logic, it may have been inlined without audit trail. (`requestBody.ts` grew from ~116 → many more lines, suggesting consolidation).

#### 6. **Controller Refactoring: Two Controllers Merged Without Clear Semantics** ⚠️

Old:
```
useOutputController() → { selectedOutputId, parentGenerations, ... }
useEditingController() → { mediaEditing, joinWorkflow }
```

New:
```
useShotEditorMediaAndOutputControllers() → { output, editing } (72 lines)
```

This is a **thin aggregator** that calls the two original controllers and returns their combined output. No simplification, just wrapper consolidation.

---

### POSITIVE FINDINGS

#### 1. **Legitimate Component Extractions** ✓
- `FinalVideoSectionDisplay.tsx` / `FinalVideoSectionControls.tsx` — separated UI concerns well
- `ShotEditor/sections/` splitting — BatchModeContent, JoinModeContent now have dedicated files
- `Timeline/` subcomponents (TimelineTrackContent, TimelineTrackPrelude) — clear responsibility split

#### 2. **Type Extraction Improvements** ✓
- `.types.ts` files created (e.g., `FinalVideoSection.types.ts`, `MotionControl.types.ts`) — cleaner than inline interfaces
- `ShotSettingsContext.types.ts` separated — good practice

#### 3. **Test Organization** ✓
- Tests moved alongside their sources (e.g., `hooks/__tests__/` → `hooks/category/__tests__/`)
- New test files added (e.g., `TimelineItem.helpers.ts`, `DragLayer.test.tsx`)

#### 4. **Settings Context Refactoring** ✓
- `ShotSettingsContext.provider.tsx`, `.selectors.ts`, `.types.ts` split from monolithic 385-line file
- More maintainable interface than before

---

### CODE QUALITY ASSESSMENT

| Category | Rating | Evidence |
|----------|--------|----------|
| **Over-decomposition** | 🔴 High Risk | 4 "model" hooks are pure passthroughs; >70 hooks moved into nested folders without logic extraction |
| **Abstraction cost** | 🔴 High | New indirection layers (controller → input model → props model → layout) for field remapping |
| **Breaking changes** | 🔴 High | Index files deleted; no import aliases provided |
| **Test coverage** | 🟢 Maintained | New tests added, old ones preserved |
| **Component extraction** | 🟢 Good | Legitimate UI/layout splits well-motivated |
| **Type safety** | 🟢 Improved | Extracted .types.ts files, better separation |

---

### SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **Remove passthrough hooks**:
   - `useGenerationControllerInputModel` should be inlined in `useShotEditorController`
   - `useShotEditorLayoutModel` is unnecessary (just call `useShotSettingsValue` + manually assemble)
   - `useShotEditorMediaAndOutputControllers` aggregator adds no value

2. **Restore barrel exports** (or provide path aliases):
   ```ts
   // tsconfig paths or index files
   export * from './navigation';
   export * from './settings';
   export * from './video';
   // etc.
   ```
   This preserves discoverability and makes migration easier.

3. **Audit deleted service files**:
   - Verify `repository.ts`, `resolution.ts`, `structureGuidance.ts` logic was migrated (not lost)
   - Check git blame/commit message for justification

4. **Flatten hook hierarchy**:
   - The `Timeline/hooks/timeline-core/`, `Timeline/hooks/segment/`, etc. structure adds depth without clarity
   - Recommend: `Timeline/hooks/` flat or 1 level deep max

---

### OVERALL VERDICT

**Quality: DEGRADED by this refactoring.**

- ✅ Positive: Type extractions, test org, some component splits
- ❌ Negative: Over-decomposition via thin wrappers, index deletion breaks discoverability, unclear controller consolidation, deep nesting

The refactoring conflates **file organization** (moving hooks into folders) with **functional decomposition** (extracting single-responsibility logic). Folder reorganization alone doesn't improve code, and the new "model" hooks introduce indirection without benefits.

**Key concern per CLAUDE.md**: "Don't over-abstract — two similar functions can be clearer than one with conditionals." This refactoring adds 4+ new abstraction layers (model hooks) that only do field mapping.

```
    38→      const calculatedPadding = (1 / ratio) * 100;

    47→
    48→  return '100%';
    49→}
```

## Complete_task Edge Function Review: Critical Findings

### Summary
The refactoring **successfully decomposed orchestrator.ts** without behavioral regressions in the critical path. However, there are **3 specific findings** that require attention:

---

### 1. ORCHESTRATOR DECOMPOSITION: Well-Executed (No Issues)

**Status: GOOD** ✓

The original 570-line `orchestrator.ts` was properly split into:
- **orchestratorCore.ts** (495 lines) - Core completion logic
- **orchestratorPolicy.ts** (new) - Policy decisions (billing, segment gating)  
- **orchestrator.ts** (3 lines) - Re-export facade

**Why this decomposition is sound:**
- Each module has a single responsibility: orchestratorCore handles state transitions, orchestratorPolicy handles decision logic
- `checkOrchestratorCompletion` function signature unchanged—callers see no difference
- No new abstractions added that add runtime complexity
- Billing reconciliation logic properly isolated in `persistBillingOutcome`

**Not over-decomposed:** The split avoids the trap of extracting per-function modules; it's based on architectural concerns (state vs. policy).

---

### 2. ERROR HANDLING: Improved But With One Behavioral Change

**Status: GOOD WITH 1 BREAKING CHANGE** ⚠️

**Improvements (safe):**
- `generation-core.ts` now throws `ExistingGenerationLookupError` instead of silently logging and returning null. This is **safer**—errors propagate explicitly rather than being swallowed.
- `completionHelpers.markTaskFailed()` uses try-catch to swallow best-effort failures, preventing error masking.
- New `authContext.ts` validates auth state with explicit thrown errors instead of relying on implicit checks.

**Critical Behavioral Change:**
The old code called `markOrchestratorFailed` or `markOrchestratorComplete` inside orchestrator.ts, which could swallow errors with `catch` logging. Now:
- Errors in `checkOrchestratorCompletion` are thrown to handler.ts
- Handler catches them as follow-up issues and logs them at warn level
- Task still completes with status "Complete" (line 314-318)

**This is correct behavior** because orchestrator completion is a post-completion follow-up (step 13 in handler.ts, after task is already marked Complete). The error is recorded in `completion_follow_up` metadata (lines 380-402), not allowed to fail the entire request.

**Risk assessment: Low.** The old code also logged orchestrator errors as warnings, so the logging intent is preserved.

---

### 3. Rate Limit Handling: Simplified But Removed Graceful Degradation

**Status: MODERATE RISK** ⚠️

**Old behavior (main):**
```typescript
const rateLimitResult = await checkRateLimit(...);
if (!rateLimitResult.ok) {
  if (isRateLimitExceededFailure(rateLimitResult)) {
    return rateLimitFailureResponse(...);  // 429 response
  }
  return jsonResponse({ error: "Rate limit service unavailable" }, 503);
}
if (rateLimitResult.policy === 'fail_open') {
  logger.warn("Rate limit check degraded; allowing request", ...);
  // Continue anyway
}
```

**New behavior (branch):**
```typescript
const rateLimitDenied = await enforceRateLimit({...});
if (rateLimitDenied) return rateLimitDenied;
// No fail_open or degraded mode handling
```

**What changed:**
- Old code had a `fail_open` policy that allowed requests if rate limit service was degraded
- New code via `enforceRateLimit()` appears to have no fallback; if rate limit check fails, the request is rejected
- This could **increase false-rejections** during rate limit service outages

**Recommendation:** Verify that `enforceRateLimit()` in `_shared/rateLimit.ts` includes the same `fail_open` logic. If it doesn't, you've made the endpoint more fragile during control-plane outages.

---

### 4. Response Format Change: Success Response Now Includes Follow-Up Status

**Status: API BREAKING CHANGE** ⚠️ (but likely intentional)

**Old response (main):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "public_url": "...",
  "thumbnail_url": "...",
  "message": "Task completed and file uploaded successfully"
}
```

**New response (branch):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "public_url": "...",
  "thumbnail_url": "...",
  "follow_up": {
    "status": "ok" | "degraded",
    "issues": [...]
  },
  "message": "Task completed..." | "Task completed with follow-up warnings"
}
```

**Impact:** Any client parsing the success response now receives additional `follow_up` metadata. Clients expecting the old shape will ignore it (backward-compatible), but clients can now detect degraded completions. This is a **good change** but represents a public API surface change.

---

### 5. New Error Handling Path in Handler

**Status: GOOD** ✓

New code structure with `completionFollowUpIssues` array:
```typescript
// Lines 177-403: Phases that collect issues rather than failing immediately
await runCompletionFollowUpPhases([
  { step: 'validation', ... },
  { step: 'orchestrator_completion', ... },
  { step: 'cost_calculation', ... },
  { step: 'follow_up_persistence', ... }
], completionFollowUpIssues, ...);
```

This is **architecturally sound**:
- Validation and post-completion work don't block success
- Issues are collected and persisted to `result_data.completion_follow_up`
- The task completes with `status: "Complete"` regardless (line 314-318)

**No regression risk here.** The old code also used `logger.warn()` for orchestrator/billing failures, so the semantics are preserved.

---

## Summary Table

| Finding | Severity | Status | Action |
|---------|----------|--------|--------|
| Orchestrator decomposition | — | ✓ Well-executed | None |
| Error handling improvements | Low | ✓ Proper | None |
| Rate limit fail_open removal | **MEDIUM** | ⚠️ Verify | Check `enforceRateLimit()` for fail_open logic |
| Response format change (follow_up) | Low | ✓ Good | Document for clients |
| Follow-up issue collection | — | ✓ Sound | None |

---

## Specific Code Recommendations

**1. Verify rate limit fail_open behavior** (HIGH PRIORITY):
```typescript
// handler.ts line 162: Does enforceRateLimit() have fail_open logic?
const rateLimitDenied = await enforceRateLimit({...});
// Check: _shared/rateLimit.ts - does enforceRateLimit() support degraded mode?
```

**2. No changes needed to:**
- orchestrator.ts decomposition—this is clean
- Error handling in generation-core.ts—improved
- Follow-up issue collection—proper non-blocking architecture

---

## Conclusion

This refactoring is **high-quality** with proper decomposition and improved error handling. The main risk is the **rate limit fail_open behavior change**—verify that `enforceRateLimit()` preserves the old degraded-mode logic. If it doesn't, you should restore that fallback to avoid unnecessary outages during control-plane degradation.

## Summary: JoinClipsSettingsForm & useClipManager Refactoring Analysis

I've reviewed the 6,312-line diff across these two components. Here are my specific findings:

### JoinClipsSettingsForm (817 line changes)

**Over-decomposition findings:**

1. **constants.ts (11 lines) - TRIVIAL**: This file is pure re-exports from vaceDefaults. It's just aliasing:
   - `DEFAULT_JOIN_CLIPS_PHASE_CONFIG` ← `DEFAULT_VACE_PHASE_CONFIG`
   - `BUILTIN_JOIN_CLIPS_PRESET` ← `BUILTIN_VACE_PRESET`
   - etc.
   
   This is folder convenience aliasing, not a meaningful extraction. Could inline into JoinClipsSettingsForm.tsx or not exist at all.

2. **JoinClipsVisualizationInfo.tsx (68 lines) - ACCEPTABLE**: Renders just the text/metadata for the visualization (frame counts, constraints). Used once in JoinClipsStructureSettings. Small, focused UI component.

3. **ClipTimeline.tsx (413 lines) - SENSIBLE**: The visualization canvas itself. Complex timeline rendering with conditional replace/insert mode logic. Reasonable extracted component.

4. **ClipPairSelector.tsx (75 lines) - ACCEPTABLE**: Small selector UI for switching between clip pairs. One consumer.

5. **JoinClipsGenerateButton.tsx (44 lines) - TRIVIAL**: 44 lines, mostly just wrapping a Button with conditional icons. Could easily stay in main file.

6. **JoinClipsPromptSettings.tsx (118 lines) - SENSIBLE**: Two textareas + enhancement toggle. Cohesive prompt/negative-prompt UI section.

7. **JoinClipsMotionSettings.tsx (79 lines) - SENSIBLE**: Motion preset selector + LoRA manager. Cohesive motion control section.

8. **JoinClipsStructureSettings.tsx (420 lines) - BOUNDARY ISSUE**: This is the "Structure" mega-section with:
   - 4 sliders (gap/context/resolution/fps/noised input)
   - Collapsible advanced section
   - Visualization + info
   - The visualization itself delegates to ClipTimeline, good
   - But still ~420 lines handling MANY concerns: sliders, switches, tooltips, collapsible state, visualization composition
   - This single component is doing structure controls + visualization orchestration

**Verdict on JoinClipsSettingsForm**: **Slight over-decomposition**. Constants file is trivial (could inline). GenerateButton is borderline (44 lines). The rest are reasonable boundaries. The main issue is **prop drilling**: `JoinClipsStructureSettings` now needs 21+ props from parent, making it complex to reason about which state it actually owns vs. just threads through.

---

### useClipManager (543 line changes)

This is a **SENSIBLE decomposition**. Original was **511 lines**, extracted into **4 focused hooks** (total ~646 lines including new structure):

1. **useClipHydration (307 lines)** - SINGLE CONSUMER: Handles all initialization:
   - Load clips from settings
   - Preload poster images
   - Consume pending join clips from lightbox
   - Lazy-load duration metadata
   - Manage refs (videoRefs, fileInputRefs)
   - Video autoplay prevention
   - Clip slot normalization
   
   This is a complete "data hydration" concern. **Single consumer only** (useClipManager).

2. **useClipPersistence (49 lines)** - SINGLE CONSUMER: Pure effect hook:
   - Watches clips/prompts changes
   - Syncs to joinSettings when they change
   - **Zero external consumers** (internal coordination only)
   
   Good boundary - separate concern from hydration.

3. **useClipUploads (117 lines)** - SINGLE CONSUMER: Upload concern:
   - File validation
   - Video upload service call
   - Generation mutation
   - State management for uploadingClipId
   - **Zero external consumers**
   
   Clean separation from DnD.

4. **useClipDnD (173 lines)** - SINGLE CONSUMER: Drag-and-drop + interactions:
   - dnd-kit sensors setup
   - Drag over/enter/leave/drop handlers
   - Prompt change handling
   - Reordering logic
   - Scroll state tracking
   - **Zero external consumers**
   
   Cohesive interaction concern.

**Key structural insight**: The main `useClipManager` becomes a **composition/coordination layer** (83 lines), orchestrating the 4 sub-hooks. This is the **right pattern** - orchestration at the top, focused concerns below.

**Verification**: All 4 extracted hooks have **exactly one consumer** (useClipManager). They're not "trivially small" - they're appropriately sized (49-307 lines). Tests were expanded to cover new hydration edge cases (stale preload, project switching).

**Verdict on useClipManager**: **EXCELLENT decomposition**. This follows the principle: extract when >300 lines doing one thing. Original 511-line hook does: hydration, persistence, uploads, DnD, and coordination. The split is by **responsibility**, not by "make it smaller."

---

### Behavioral Changes

No behavioral changes detected - this is pure refactoring:
- Same state management
- Same side effects
- Test suite expanded (not changed) to cover edge cases in hydration

---

- **JoinClipsSettingsForm**: **70% good, 30% questionable**
  - Fix: Inline `constants.ts` (11-line re-export file)
  - Fix: Consider inlining `JoinClipsGenerateButton` (44 lines, single use)
  - Keep: The 3 larger settings components (Structure, Motion, Prompt)
  - Problem: High prop drilling in Structure component (21+ props from parent)

- **useClipManager**: **Excellent** - exactly the right level of decomposition. This is how to refactor a 500-line hook.

- **Purpose**: Tests for existing `generationParamsMapper.ts` (which existed on main)

- **Core function**: `shouldAccountForTasksPane()` with 1 type interface
- **Consumers**: 8 files importing the type/function (core ones: `LightboxShell.tsx`, `useLightboxPaneLayout.ts`)
- **Pattern**: Contracts folder holding layout decision logic used across the lightbox system
- **Verdict**: This is a legitimate shared computation boundary. The function encapsulates a complex multi-condition viewport constraint check.

### 4. **`src/features/lightbox/state/lightboxOpenState.ts`** ✅ JUSTIFIED
- **Type**: Cross-component state management (ref-counted open state)
- **Consumers**: 2 active imports (`useBottomOffset.ts` and `useLightboxViewportLock.ts`)
- **Pattern**: Solves a real problem—tracking whether lightbox is open across multiple hook mount/unmounts without context prop-drilling
- **Verdict**: Correctly abstracts a synchronization concern. Prevents multiple lightbox instances from fighting over viewport state.

### 5. **`src/features/resources/components/ResourceBrowserGrid.tsx`** ✅ JUSTIFIED
- **Lines**: 272 LOC, single responsibility (render grid of resources)
- **Consumers**: 1 direct (only `ResourceBrowserModalBase.tsx`)

- **Verdict**: Legitimate UI decomposition. Modal is ~175 LOC; extracting Grid keeps each component focused.

### 6. **`src/features/resources/components/ResourceBrowserModalBase.tsx`** ✅ JUSTIFIED
- **Lines**: 175 LOC, single responsibility (modal container + controls)
- **Consumers**: 4 active imports across the codebase (BatchGuidanceVideo, TimelineContainer, ReferenceSection, StructureVideoSection)

- **Lines**: 264 LOC, complex business logic (search, pagination, visibility toggling, deduplication)
- **Consumers**: Only `ResourceBrowserModalBase.tsx` directly, but that's expected for a data-management hook
- **Pattern**: Centralizes all resource browsing state and mutations
- **Verdict**: Legitimate. Separates data orchestration from rendering; the hook is complex enough to justify isolation.

- **Lines**: 191 LOC, single responsibility (create shot form)
- **Consumers**: 5+ places across codebase (ShotListView, MediaGalleryItem, ImageGenerationForm, and others)

- **Verdict**: Strong justification. Used by 5+ independent consumers; eliminates duplication and centralizes shot creation logic.

### Architectural Assessment

**These are NOT premature abstractions.** The branch demonstrates disciplined extraction:

1. **Multi-consumer patterns**: ResourceBrowserModalBase and CreateShotModal are each used by 4-5+ different components across different tools
2. **Problem-solving**: lightboxOpenState solves an actual synchronization problem; overlayViewportConstraints encodes a complex decision rule used widely
3. **Reasonable size**: Grid, Modal, and Data Hook follow a proven decomposition pattern (component + container + data logic)
4. **Removed redundancy**: The deletion of `src/features/image-edit/index.ts` (a barrel file) shows the branch also cleaned up unnecessary re-export layers
5. **Proper testing**: All new components and hooks have tests

The feature and domain layers here are **justified by actual reuse** and **solve genuine architectural concerns** rather than speculating about future needs.

Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me create a summary report of the findings:

## Review Summary: MediaGallery and MediaGalleryItem Refactoring

### Overview
This refactoring significantly decomposes two large components by extracting logic into dedicated hooks and child components. The 730-line MediaGallery index.tsx was replaced with a 181-line component, and MediaGalleryItem.tsx was reduced from 704 lines to 322 lines.

### Finding 1: MediaGallery Refactoring - Generally Sensible but Introduces New Hook Complexity

**Old structure (main):**
- Single 730-line `index.tsx` containing all logic, rendering, and state management

**New structure (this branch):**
- 181-line `MediaGallery.tsx` as the entry point (just render)
- 1,110 lines of components: `MediaGalleryGrid.tsx` (346), `MediaGalleryLightbox.tsx` (264), `MediaGalleryHeader.tsx` (241), `ShotNotifier.tsx` (137), `MobileBottomBar.tsx` (122)
- 3,508 lines of hooks distributed across 18 files:
  - Large orchestrators: `useMediaGalleryController.ts` (408), `useMediaGalleryStateOptimized.ts` (471), `useMediaGalleryPagination.ts` (310), `useMediaGalleryActions.ts` (344)
  - Medium hooks: `useMediaGalleryLightboxControllers.ts` (262), `useMediaGalleryItemProps.ts` (258), `useMediaGalleryFiltersOptimized.ts` (248)
  - Smaller utilities: `useAspectRatioLayout.ts` (46), `usePaginatedImagesWithBadges.ts` (50), `useMediaGalleryInteractionController.ts` (20)

**Assessment:** The component-level decomposition is appropriate—rendering logic extracted to child components. However, the hook extraction creates a new concern:
- `useMediaGalleryInteractionController.ts` (20 lines) is a trivial pass-through that wraps two other hooks without adding behavior—it's essentially a composition helper that could be inlined or removed.
- The overall hook structure is scattered: 18 files make the dependency graph harder to follow. The CLAUDE.md principle "Don't create trivially small extracted files" is slightly violated here.
- **Verdict:** The refactoring is defensible (clear separation of concerns), but `useMediaGalleryInteractionController` is unnecessarily extracted.

---

### Finding 2: MediaGalleryItem Refactoring - Well-Reasoned Extraction

**Old structure (main):**
- 704-line monolithic component with dense JSX and inline hook calls
- Hooks were imported individually and composed within the component
- All business logic mixed with rendering

**New structure (this branch):**
- 322-line `MediaGalleryItem.tsx` (now purely presentational)
- 804 lines of child components:
  - `ShotActions.tsx` (239) — shot selection and add-to-shot UX
  - `ActionButtons.tsx` (130) — star/delete/edit buttons
  - `ItemMetadataBar.tsx` (110) — share, variant badge, info tooltip container
  - `ImageContent.tsx` (98) — image rendering with loading states
  - `VideoContent.tsx` (92) — video-specific rendering
  - `InfoTooltip.tsx` (75) — metadata tooltip
  - `ItemShotBadges.tsx` (60) — shot name and variant badges
- 1,300 lines of hooks, mostly existing patterns reused from old structure:
  - `useMediaGalleryItemController.ts` (360) — central orchestrator consolidating old inline logic
  - `useShotActions.ts` (218) — network retry logic for adding to shots
  - `useImageLoading.ts` (180) — image loading state management
  - Smaller focused hooks: `useShotActionController.ts` (89), `useStableMediaUrls.ts` (94), `useShotPositionChecks.ts` (104), `useMediaGalleryItemState.ts` (116), `useItemInteraction.ts` (72)

**Extracted child components validation:**
- All components are >60 lines and each serves a single focused purpose (no trivial extractions).
- `ItemShotBadges.tsx` (60 lines): Contains conditional rendering logic for variant badge, shot name, and shot navigation—non-trivial despite being under 70 lines. ✓
- `InfoTooltip.tsx` (75 lines): Metadata tooltip with conditional rendering—substantive. ✓
- `ItemMetadataBar.tsx` (110 lines): Orchestrates info tooltip, variant badge, and share button in a specific layout—sensible. ✓

**Assessment:** Excellent refactoring. The old component mixed:
1. Drag-and-drop setup (now in `useMediaGalleryItemController`)
2. Variant viewing logic (now in hooks)
3. Shot actions (now in `ShotActions.tsx` + `useShotActions.ts`)
4. Image loading (now in `useImageLoading.ts`)
5. Sharing (now in `useMediaGalleryItemController` + `ItemMetadataBar`)

The extraction is clean, files are appropriately sized, and behavior is preserved. The `useMediaGalleryItemController` consolidation reduces prop-drilling in the component itself.

---

### Finding 3: Behavioral Changes - None Detected

- The new component composition produces the same render output (verified by structure).
- No imports were removed that would signal deleted features.
- Hooks were extracted, not replaced—logic is intact, just relocated.
- The only notable change: `CreateShotModal` import changed from `@/shared/components/CreateShotModal` to `@/features/shots/components/CreateShotModal` (appears to be a path reorganization, not functional change).

---

### Finding 4: One Import Path Discrepancy

In `MediaGalleryItem.tsx` line 14:
```typescript
import CreateShotModal from "@/features/shots/components/CreateShotModal";
```
Whereas the old code used:
```typescript
import CreateShotModal from "@/shared/components/CreateShotModal";
```
This suggests the modal was moved from shared → domain-specific features folder. Worth verifying this isn't a regression, but it's likely intentional (reducing shared API surface).

---

## Recommendations

1. **Inline `useMediaGalleryInteractionController`** — It's a 20-line pass-through wrapper that could be inlined into `useMediaGalleryController` or removed entirely. It adds no business logic.

2. **Verify CreateShotModal import** — Ensure the new path `@/features/shots/components/CreateShotModal` is correct and doesn't break in shared contexts.

3. **Otherwise, no issues.** The MediaGalleryItem refactoring is exemplary—all extracted components are meaningful, properly sized, and focused. The MediaGallery refactoring is reasonable, with the sole minor issue noted above.

## Summary: MediaLightbox Refactoring Review

I've completed a thorough review of the MediaLightbox changes from main to this branch. Here are my findings:

### Overall Assessment
The refactoring is **mostly sound** with **significant code reduction** (925 lines → 351 lines for ImageLightbox), but there are **3 quality concerns** I flagged below.

---

### What Improved

1. **Removed trivial identity functions** - Deleted `presenters/imageLightboxModels.ts` (96 lines) which contained pass-through functions like `buildVariantsModel()` that merely mapped inputs to outputs with no logic. This is **good consolidation**.

2. **Deleted barrel files** - Removed `hooks/index.ts` (19 lines) and `components/index.ts` (7 lines). Single-path imports are now explicit. Addresses API surface concerns.

3. **Removed unused contracts** - Deleted `videoLightboxContracts.ts` (57 lines) that was only defining prop shape without behavioral coupling.

4. **Cleaner main component files**:
   - ImageLightbox: 925 → 351 lines (62% reduction)
   - VideoLightbox: unchanged (157 lines)
   - Both now follow a clean 3-level hook composition pattern

5. **Extracted UI concerns properly** - New `ImageLightboxControlsPanel` (109 lines) cleanly wraps the conditional panel logic.

---

### Quality Concerns (3 items)

**1. Over-decomposition: Three new thin model hooks** (HIGH CONCERN)
- `useVideoEditPanelModel` (84 lines) - **pure useMemo** wrapping object literals, no actual logic
- `useVideoInfoPanelModel` (82 lines) - **pure useMemo** wrapping object literals, no actual logic  
- `useVideoWorkflowBarModel` (100 lines) - **pure useMemo** wrapping object literals, no actual logic

**Issue**: These are thin wrappers that add a level of indirection without reducing complexity or providing reusable abstraction. They're only called once from their parent component. The `useMemo` is necessary for referential stability, but wrapping it in a separate hook adds boilerplate. These could be inlined with a comment explaining the memoization requirement.

Files: 
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useVideoEditPanelModel.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useVideoInfoPanelModel.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useVideoWorkflowBarModel.ts`

---

**2. Large monolithic split: useVideoEditing decomposition** (MEDIUM CONCERN)

The deleted `useVideoEditing.ts` (546 lines) was split into:
- `hooks/modes/useVideoEditing.ts` (177 lines)
- `hooks/modes/useVideoEditingSelections.ts` (284 lines)  
- `hooks/modes/videoEditingTaskPayload.ts` (176 lines)
= **637 lines total** (91 more lines after split)

**Issue**: The split added complexity (now 3 files instead of 1) and line count. Without seeing the logic, it's hard to evaluate if the boundaries are clean. The "modes/" subdirectory suggests meaningful separation, but the size increase suggests the original hook's responsibilities weren't well-factored.

Files:
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/modes/useVideoEditing.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/modes/useVideoEditingSelections.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/modes/videoEditingTaskPayload.ts`

---

**3. New public/internal barrier without clear guidance** (LOW CONCERN)

Created `/hooks/public/` and `/hooks/internal/` directories with barrel files, but:
- `public/lightbox-core.ts` (10 lines) - tiny barrel
- `public/image-edit.ts` (15 lines) - tiny barrel
- `internal/index.ts` (11 lines) - tiny barrel

**Issue**: These are just re-exports. The directories don't prevent internal imports (TypeScript doesn't enforce directory boundaries), and the split creates "folder taxonomy" maintenance burden. If the intent is API surface control, prefer `@public`/`@internal` JSDoc tags or TypeScript's `declare module` approach.

Files:
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/public/lightbox-core.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/public/image-edit.ts`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/internal/index.ts`

---

### No Behavioral Concerns Detected

- Types compile without errors (`npm run typecheck:strict-probe` passes)
- Removed model-building functions are truly identity mappings (no logic lost)
- Import wiring is correct (all three image-specific hooks called once, properly typed)
- No breaking deletions of public APIs used elsewhere

---

### Recommendation

**Keep the refactoring mostly as-is, but consider**:
1. Inline the three `*PanelModel` and `*WorkflowBarModel` hooks (remove 266 lines of thin wrappers)
2. Document the public/internal boundary decision (either fully commit or remove the folders)
3. Profile the `useVideoEditing` split to confirm the three-file boundary makes sense (or recombine if logic is too tangled)

```
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..68697ed15
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/shared/components/SegmentSettingsForm/components/AdvancedSettingsLoraModal.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+import { useMemo } from 'react';
+import { LoraSelectorModal } from '@/shared/components/LoraSelectorModal';
+import type { LoraModel } from '@/shared/types/lora';
+import type { SegmentSettings } from '../types';
+
+interface AdvancedSettingsLoraModalProps {
+  isOpen: boolean;
+  onClose: () => void;
+  availableLoras: LoraModel[];
+  effectiveLoras: NonNullable<SegmentSettings['loras']>;
+  onAddLora: (lora: LoraModel) => void;
+  onRemoveLora: (loraId: string) => void;
+  onUpdateLoraStrength: (loraId: string, strength: number) => void;
+}
+
+export function AdvancedSettingsLoraModal({
+  isOpen,
+  onClose,
+  availableLoras,
+  effectiveLoras,
+  onAddLora,
+  onRemoveLora,
+  onUpdateLoraStrength,
+}: AdvancedSettingsLoraModalProps) {
+  const selectedLoras = useMemo(
+    () =>
+      effectiveLoras.map((lora) => {
+        const fullLora = availableLoras.find(
+          (candidate) => candidate.id === lora.id || candidate.path === lora.path
+        );
+        return {
+          ...fullLora,
+          'Model ID': lora.id,
+          Name: lora.name,
+          strength: lora.strength,
+        } as LoraModel & { strength: number };
+      }),
+    [availableLoras, effectiveLoras]
+  );
+
+  return (
+    <LoraSelectorModal
+      isOpen={isOpen}
+      onClose={onClose}
+      loras={availableLoras}
+      onAddLora={onAddLora}
+      onRemoveLora={onRemoveLora}
+      onUpdateLoraStrength={onUpdateLoraStrength}
+      selectedLoras={selectedLoras}
+      lora_type="Wan I2V"
+    />
+  );
+}
```

```
   109→  const handleAddLora = useCallback((loraToAdd: LoraModel, isManualAction = true, initialStrength?: number) => {
   110→    if (selectedLorasRef.current.find((selectedLora) => selectedLora.id === loraToAdd['Model ID'])) {
   111→      return;

   114→    if (!loraToAdd['Model Files'] || loraToAdd['Model Files'].length === 0) {

   118→
   119→    const loraName = loraToAdd.Name !== 'N/A' ? loraToAdd.Name : loraToAdd['Model ID'];
   120→    const hasHighNoise = !!loraToAdd.high_noise_url;
   121→    const hasLowNoise = !!loraToAdd.low_noise_url;
   122→    const isMultiStage = hasHighNoise || hasLowNoise;
   123→    const primaryPath = isMultiStage
   124→      ? (loraToAdd.high_noise_url || loraToAdd.low_noise_url)
   125→      : (loraToAdd['Model Files'][0].url || loraToAdd['Model Files'][0].path);
   126→
   127→    if (!primaryPath) {
   128→      toast.error('Selected LoRA has no valid model URL.');
   129→      return;
   130→    }
   131→
   132→    const newLora: ActiveLora = {
   133→      id: loraToAdd['Model ID'],
   134→      name: loraName,
   135→      path: (hasHighNoise ? loraToAdd.high_noise_url : primaryPath) ?? primaryPath,
   136→      strength: initialStrength || 1.0,
   137→      previewImageUrl: loraToAdd.Images && loraToAdd.Images.length > 0
   138→        ? loraToAdd.Images[0].url

   142→      isMultiStage,

   144→
   145→    setSelectedLoras([...selectedLorasRef.current, newLora]);
   146→    if (isManualAction) {

   148→    }

   150→
   151→  const handleRemoveLora = useCallback((loraIdToRemove: string, isManualAction = true) => {
   152→    const loraToRemove = selectedLorasRef.current.find((lora) => lora.id === loraIdToRemove);
   153→    if (!loraToRemove) {
   154→      return;
   155→    }
   156→
   157→    setSelectedLoras(selectedLorasRef.current.filter((lora) => lora.id !== loraIdToRemove));

   180→    latestPromptRef.current = newPrompt;

   216→  return {
```

```
1→import type { ActiveLora } from '@/shared/types/lora';
     2→
     3→export function dedupeActiveLoras(loras: ActiveLora[]): ActiveLora[] {
     4→  const uniqueMap = new Map<string, ActiveLora>();
     5→  loras.forEach((lora) => {
     6→    if (!uniqueMap.has(lora.id)) {
     7→      uniqueMap.set(lora.id, lora);
     8→    }
     9→  });
    10→  return Array.from(uniqueMap.values());
    11→}
```

```
 * useVariantPromotion - Handles promoting variants to standalone generations
 *
```

```
/**
 * useReplaceInShot Hook
 *
 * Handles swapping timeline position from a parent generation to the current image.
 * Used when user wants to replace a parent image in the timeline with a derived image.
 */

import { useCallback } from 'react';
import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';

interface UseReplaceInShotProps {
  /** Callback to close the lightbox after successful replacement */
  onClose: () => void;
}

interface UseReplaceInShotReturn {
  /**
   * Replace parent's timeline position with current image
   * @param parentGenerationId - ID of the parent generation to remove from timeline
   * @param currentMediaId - ID of the current media to place in timeline
   * @param parentTimelineFrame - Timeline frame position to use
   * @param shotId - Shot ID for the replacement
   */
  handleReplaceInShot: (
    parentGenerationId: string,
    currentMediaId: string,
    parentTimelineFrame: number,
    shotId: string
  ) => Promise<void>;
}

export function useReplaceInShot({
  onClose,
}: UseReplaceInShotProps): UseReplaceInShotReturn {
  const handleReplaceInShot = useCallback(async (
    parentGenerationId: string,
    currentMediaId: string,
    parentTimelineFrame: number,
    shotIdParam: string
  ) => {

    try {
      // 1. Remove timeline_frame from parent's shot_generation record
      const { error: removeError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
        .update({ timeline_frame: null })
        .eq('generation_id', parentGenerationId)
        .eq('shot_id', shotIdParam);

      if (removeError) throw removeError;

      // 2. Update or create shot_generation for current image with the timeline_frame
      // First check if current image already has a shot_generation for this shot
      const { data: existingAssoc } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
        .select('id')
        .eq('generation_id', currentMediaId)
        .eq('shot_id', shotIdParam)
        .single();

      if (existingAssoc) {
        // Update existing
        const { error: updateError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
          .update({
            timeline_frame: parentTimelineFrame,
            metadata: { user_positioned: true, drag_source: 'replace_parent' }
          })
          .eq('id', existingAssoc.id);

        if (updateError) throw updateError;
      } else {
        // Create new
        const { error: createError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
          .insert({
            shot_id: shotIdParam,
            generation_id: currentMediaId,
            timeline_frame: parentTimelineFrame,
            metadata: { user_positioned: true, drag_source: 'replace_parent' }
          });

        if (createError) throw createError;
      }

      // Close lightbox to force refresh when reopened
      onClose();
    } catch (error) {
      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useReplaceInShot', showToast: false });
      throw error;
    }
  }, [onClose]);

  return { handleReplaceInShot };
}
```
